the database server is a very demanding workload that can be characterized by a set of key characteristics, which are then used to identify a set of OS features that can be used to improve its performance.
the database engine and its interaction with the OS are extremely complex.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the database engine is very sensitive to the OS environment, and the OS is not always able to provide the desired level of support.
the OS plays a critical role in the performance of a database server and that the performance of the database engine is strongly influenced by the OS characteristics.
the database engine is a significant source of overhead for the OS.

there is a lot of scope for improving the performance of these applications through better OS support, and we believe that this is a worthwhile direction for future research.
the database engine and operating system interact at many levels, and a holistic view of this interaction is needed to understand the behavior of the system.
